title: Gemba account sprintpad — Jamal's QBR & renewal scratchpad
content:
Quick context: account is mid-market e-comm platform (three apps). Renewal window = 2026-07-20. Primary champion: Laura Meyers (CTO). Secondary champion: Raj Patel (platform). Renewal ask: move from hosted -> dedicated plus 12-mo commit. Current ARR approx $72k/year.

TODAY (sprint):
- Finalize QBR slide skeleton by noon (3 slides: health, usage/cost, roadmap ask).
- Pull per-route latency + token spend for last 90 days (billing/export ticket JIRA-CS-8910).
- Confirm demo unit for canary rollback: setup dedicated zone with 2x burst nodes (ask infra SEA).
- Send pre-read to Laura + Raj today EOD (concise: 1 page executive + 3 bullets).

Top risks (short):
- Cost surprise: spike in recommendation reranks in May (look at prefix cache hit %).
- Champion bandwidth: Laura travels 7/5-7/12 — need decision before travel.
- SRE concerns: customer wants audit logs retention 1y (private-deploy option).

QBR talking points (bulletable):
- Opening: 30s — quick thank you, highlight 6m adoption trends.
- Health: 99.95% success, P95 latency improved 18% after batching change (May 10).
- Cost: unit cost down 22% when routed to quantized variant; projected savings $18k/yr if committed.
- Reliability ask: propose Dedicated (reserved) with SLA and 4h incident response add-on.
- Compliance ask: discuss Private deployment option for audit logs + KMS integration.

Demo script (3 mins):
1) Show live inference on staging (low latency path). Quick compare: hosted vs dedicated (latency & RU).
2) Walk through console trace for a failed call -> automatic fallback to smaller model (show rollback).
3) Show Optimize suggestion: batching + cache predicted to recover 30% of cost without model quality hit.

Data to pull (actionable):
- Token breakdown per route (cache-hit vs miss) last 90 days (CSV).
- Top 10 failing prompts and sample outputs (for conversation quality check).
- SLA incident log for last 6 months (timestamps + resolution).

Email pre-read outline (one pager):
- One-line summary: "Recommend reserved Dedicated capacity + 12-mo commit to stabilize latency and lower unit cost."
- 3 bullets: 1) Cost math (current vs committed), 2) Reliability wins (SLA + fallbacks), 3) Timeline & next steps (trial window + kickoff).
- Attachments: sample billing delta spreadsheet, short demo gif, contract term snapshot.

Open questions / TODOs to resolve before QBR:
- Legal: confirm Private deployment minimum commitment (ask legal@redwood).
- Pricing: do we include migration credits for first 3 months? (pricing ops).
- Technical: can we guarantee egress region parity for their APAC customers? (infra).

Follow-ups after QBR (post-meeting):
- Draft PO template and send to Raj within 48h if accepted.
- Create dedicated rollout plan + canary steps (ops + infra).
- Add eval prompts to regression harness and schedule weekly quality checks for first 90 days.

Notes-to-self (rambling):
- Keep pre-read < 1 page — execs hate slides. Use table: current vs committed cost numbers.
- Laura cares about predictability (emphasize SLAs more than savings).
- Prepare optional fallback offer: 6-month trial of Dedicated with opt-out at month 3 if SLO not met.

Slack pings to send: 
- @priya: can you sanity-check the cost calc? (share sheet link)
- @hector: can you ask infra about APAC egress parity?
- #cs-onsite: flag for prepped demo laptop + network test at 8:30am day-of.

Meeting logistics:
- QBR slot: 2026-07-14 10:00 PDT (confirm via calendar invite).
- Prep run: 2026-07-13 09:00 PDT (tech check + slide run-through).

End-of-day checklist (EOD):
- [ ] Slides skeleton version 0.9 uploaded to shared folder.
- [ ] Data exports attached to pre-read.
- [ ] Slack pings done.
- [ ] Draft pre-read emailed to collaborators for review.

Free-format brain dump (misc):
- Could try framing migration as "performance assurance" rather than "cost save" — Laura will respond better.
- Mention Redwood Optimize: show a real example of batching % increase; they love numbers.
- Keep a short anecdote about a similar customer who avoided outage after fallback enabled (pull case study id).

--jamal

(quick reference: contact book -> Laura Meyers laura.m@client.com; Raj Patel raj@client.com)
